name: snmpwalk - MIB Enumeration with Community String
description: Walk the SNMP MIB tree with a validated community string to dump OS, processes, users, installed packages, network interfaces, and routing table.

variations.description: SNMPv1 walk with timeout (for slow/legacy targets)
variations.label: SNMP v1 (timeout)

variations.description: braa - bulk OID query against multiple hosts
variations.label: braa (fast OID)

examples.label: SNMPv1 walk with 10s timeout (OSCP Ch06 style)
Dump running processes (cross-reference with known services)
Dump installed packages with versions (CVE lookup)
braa bulk OID dump against host

notes: A full MIB walk against a system with a known community string yields: OS version/kernel, hostname, contact, location, uptime, boot parameters, running processes, user accounts, and installed packages with versions. HIGH-VALUE: installed package list with versions enables targeted CVE lookup without running a scanner. Contact email cross-validates infrastructure ownership with DNS SOA and cert admin email. Boot command line parameters can expose filesystem UUIDs. Key Windows OIDs: users (1.3.6.1.4.1.77.1.2.25), processes (1.3.6.1.2.1.25.4.2.1.2), installed software (1.3.6.1.2.1.25.6.3.1.2), open TCP ports (1.3.6.1.2.1.6.13.1.3). Chaining: onesixtyone → valid community string → snmpwalk system OID → package versions for CVE lookup → braa for bulk extended OID enumeration. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 6 (Information Gathering).

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Penetration Testing with Kali Linux

recommended.note: Use onesixtyone to discover a valid community string before walking the MIB.
snmp-enum card covers the combined workflow including nmap SNMP host discovery.

defense.why_it_works: SNMPv1/v2c transmits data in cleartext and uses community strings for authentication with no session expiry. Once the community string is known (bruted or sniffed), the full MIB is accessible.
defense.prerequisites: UDP 161 reachable and valid community string obtained (via onesixtyone or sniffing).
defense.misconfiguration: Community string left as default 'public'. No restriction on which OID subtrees are readable. SNMP accessible from any IP.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# snmpd.conf
rocommunity public default   # world-readable, default string
defense.secure_config:
# Upgrade to SNMPv3 auth+priv, disable v1/v2c
createUser monitor SHA 'Auth@Pass1!' AES 'Priv@Pass2!'
rouser monitor authPriv .1
# Remove all rocommunity/rwcommunity lines
defense.impact: Full system inventory: OS version, running processes, installed packages, network config, user accounts — enough to identify exploitable services without an active scanner.
defense.detection: SNMP walk generates many GET-NEXT requests in rapid succession against all OIDs. Visible in network capture or SNMP agent logs as sequential OID traversal from a single source.
defense.artifacts: Network traffic on UDP 161 with sequential OID requests. SNMP agent access log entries.
defense.prevention: Upgrade to SNMPv3. Disable SNMP if not used. Restrict SNMP to management VLAN. Audit snmpd.conf for world-readable community strings.
defense.evasion: Query specific high-value OIDs individually rather than walking the full tree to reduce request volume.
